newsitem.title: UK: RTZ continues climb on strong copper price.
newsitem.headline: RTZ continues climb on strong copper price.

text.p: Shares in RTZ Corporation Plc were up 16p to a 12-month high of 10.42 stg, only a whisker below their April 30, 1996 record closing peak of 10.45 stg amid continued strength in the price of copper, an important commodity for the mining group.
"Copper has been rocketing the past few months and has dragged up RTZ. As long as copper remains strong, RTZ will benefit," one market maker said.

RTZ has risen nearly 20 percent since February 5 when the shares closed at a 1997 low of 882-1/2p, spurred on by a sharp advance in the price of copper, a mineral from which the mining group extracts around 25 percent of its revenues.
Three months copper, which was trading at $2,481/$2,485 per tonne by 0800 GMT, up $6 from Thursday's close, has risen over $300 per tonne or 15 percent since the beginning of the year.
This week alone has seen the benchmark copper price soar nearly $100 per tonne and analysts expect further near-term gains.
